intro: The Liturgy of the Hours is the Church's daily prayer, mostly psalms, prayed at set times. Here are the two hours anyone can pray — Morning Prayer (Lauds) when you rise and Night Prayer (Compline) before bed — in a simple one-week form built from the Roman breviary: a psalm, a short reading, the Gospel canticle, the Our Father and a prayer. Psalm numbers follow the Vulgate.

canticle.n: The Benedictus — the canticle of Zechariah

otc.n: Canticle of the three young men

days.prayer: Almighty and everlasting God, who on this day opened for us the way to eternal life by your Son's victory over death: grant that we who keep the feast of his resurrection may, through the renewal of your Spirit, rise again in the light of life. Through Christ our Lord.
Lord God, fill our hearts with the light of your Holy Spirit, that we may be free from sin and rich in every good work. Through Christ our Lord.
Lord, who send the light of a new day, grant that we may spend it in your service and come at evening to praise you with a clean heart. Through Christ our Lord.
Hear our morning prayer, Lord, and let the light of your face shine on all we do this day, that our words and works may please you. Through Christ our Lord.
Almighty God, who gave us your Son to be the light of the world: scatter the darkness of our hearts, and let the day we begin in your name end in your peace. Through Christ our Lord.
Lord Jesus Christ, who at this hour were led out to the cross for the salvation of the world: forgive us our sins, and make us worthy of the price you paid. Who live and reign for ever and ever.
Lord God, source of all light, who made this day for work and the night for rest: keep us this day from every fault, that we may come at last to the day that has no evening. Through Christ our Lord.

night.examination: Pause. Look back over the day in God's presence: where was he, and where were you? Give thanks for what was good; ask pardon for what was not.

canticle.n: The Nunc dimittis — the canticle of Simeon

night.responsory: Into your hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. — Into your hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit. You have redeemed us, Lord God of truth. — I commend my spirit. Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. — Into your hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit.
night.closing: May the almighty Lord grant us a quiet night and a perfect end. Amen.

days.prayer: Lord, we have celebrated today the mystery of the rising of Christ to new life. May we now rest in your peace, safe from all that could harm us, and rise again refreshed and joyful, to praise you throughout another day. Through Christ our Lord.
Lord, give our bodies restful sleep, and let the work we have done today bear fruit in eternal life. Through Christ our Lord.
Lord, fill this night with your radiance. May we sleep in peace and rise with joy to welcome the light of a new day in your name. Through Christ our Lord.

Lord Jesus Christ, you have given your followers an example of gentleness and humility, a task that is easy, a burden that is light. Accept the prayers and work of this day, and give us the rest that will strengthen us to render more faithful service to you. Who live and reign for ever and ever.
Lord God, send peace into our hearts at the end of the day, so that we may contemplate your resurrection in silence and rise refreshed to serve you. Through Christ our Lord.
All-powerful God, keep us united with your Son in his death and burial, so that we may rise to new life with him, who lives and reigns for ever and ever.
Lord, be with us throughout this night. When day comes may we rise from sleep to rejoice in the resurrection of your Christ, who lives and reigns for ever and ever.

advent.when: from the first Sunday of Advent to the Presentation (2 February)
advent.la: Alma Redemptóris Mater, quæ pérvia cæli porta manes, et stella maris, succúrre cadénti, súrgere qui curat, pópulo: tu quæ genuísti, natúra miránte, tuum sanctum Genitórem, Virgo prius ac postérius, Gabriélis ab ore sumens illud Ave, peccatórum miserére.
advent.en: Loving Mother of the Redeemer, gate of heaven, star of the sea, assist your people who have fallen yet strive to rise again. To the wonderment of nature you bore your Creator, yet remained a virgin after as before. You who received Gabriel's joyful greeting, have pity on us poor sinners.

lent.when: from the Presentation to Wednesday of Holy Week
lent.la: Ave, Regína cælórum, ave, Dómina angelórum, salve, radix, salve, porta, ex qua mundo lux est orta. Gaude, Virgo gloriósa, super omnes speciósa; vale, o valde decóra, et pro nobis Christum exóra.
lent.en: Hail, Queen of heaven; hail, Lady of the angels. Hail, root and gate from which the Light of the world was born. Rejoice, glorious Virgin, fairest of all; farewell, most beautiful, and pray to Christ for us.

easter.la: Regína cæli, lætáre, allelúia. Quia quem meruísti portáre, allelúia, resurréxit, sicut dixit, allelúia. Ora pro nobis Deum, allelúia.
easter.en: Queen of heaven, rejoice, alleluia. For he whom you merited to bear, alleluia, has risen as he said, alleluia. Pray for us to God, alleluia.

ordinary.la: Salve, Regína, Mater misericórdiæ, vita, dulcédo et spes nostra, salve. Ad te clamámus, éxsules fílii Hevæ. Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes in hac lacrimárum valle. Eia ergo, advocáta nostra, illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte. Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui, nobis post hoc exsílium osténde. O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
ordinary.en: Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve; to thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us, and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

examen.intro: An examination of conscience for the evening, or before confession. Read slowly; stop where something stings. It follows the Ten Commandments, as the Church has done since the Fathers, and ends with the Act of Contrition.

qs: Have I put anything before God — money, comfort, my own will, another person? Have I prayed today, and did I mean it?
Have I used God's name carelessly, or sworn falsely? Have I spoken of holy things with contempt?
Have I kept Sunday holy: Mass, rest, worship, time for family? Have I made others work needlessly?
Have I honoured my parents, and cared for them in their need? Have I been patient with my children, or harsh?
Have I harmed anyone, in body or in spirit? Nursed anger, held a grudge, refused to forgive, wished someone ill?
Have I been faithful, in act and in thought, to my spouse or to my state in life? Have I used others, or looked at them as things?
Have I taken what is not mine, or kept what I owe? Have I been honest at work, and just to those who work for me? Have I given to the poor?
Have I lied, gossiped, spread what should not be spread, or stayed silent when I should have spoken? Have I judged rashly?
Have I envied what others have, or resented their good? Have I been ungrateful for what I have?
Have I been proud, vain, sulking, self-pitying? Have I been lazy where duty called, or greedy with food, drink or the screen?
Is there anyone I need to ask forgiveness of, or forgive, before I sleep?
